messages:
Jasmine Liu: Heads up — getting a small wave of inbound tickets referencing the benchmark numbers (esp EU vs us-east variance + “why did my results not match”). Anyone have a canonical explanation + public FAQ/methodology link we should paste? Want to avoid everyone ad-libbing.

Wei Chen: Yep. Public methodology page is live here: https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/methodology (includes workloads, caching/batching policy, regions, aggregation). We also have the FAQ section on the landing page: https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks#faq

Elliot Price: +1. The methodology page has the “what causes variance” callout + stability gates. If you need the shorter doc-friendly link, we also added: https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/how-we-measured (redirects to methodology).

Jasmine Liu: Perfect. What’s the recommended 2–3 sentence explanation for region variance? Tickets are basically: “EU numbers look worse than NA; is that real? can you guarantee my p95?”

Claire Dubois: Suggested canonical answer (approved in reviews):
- Region-to-region differences are expected due to network RTT, local capacity/queueing, and hardware availability.
- Our published metrics are medians across repeated runs with warmup + stability gates (we rerun when p95 variance exceeds threshold), and we report p50/p95 so readers can see tail behavior.
- For production SLOs, we recommend validating with your own prompt/context mix + concurrency; we can help set up a quick PoC and recommend Hosted vs Dedicated based on latency targets.

Soojin Lee: Adding one guardrail: please avoid “guarantee” language. Use “observed in our benchmark runs” + “we offer SLA targets on Dedicated” when appropriate. Also don’t imply competitor regions are “slow” broadly — stick to “in our measurements under defined workload.”

Renee Sullivan: Can we include one line about caching/batching? A couple of the tickets I saw are basically “did you turn on magic caching.”

Claire Dubois: Yep. We should say: “We ran with production-recommended settings (documented in methodology), including continuous batching; we did not rely on customer-specific prompt caching. All settings are published, and we provide configs/manifests for reproducibility.”

Wei Chen: The FAQ has an explicit Q: “Was caching enabled?” with that exact framing. Might be easiest to link + quote it.

Jasmine Liu: Great. I’ll turn this into a Support macro:
1) link methodology
2) 3 bullets on variance + p50/p95
3) offer PoC / Dedicated sizing if they need strict p95

Elliot Price: If you want to point people to “replicate” quickly, the public page also says: same model version + region + context length; match concurrency; run multiple trials; compare distribution not a single run.

Soojin Lee: Please include the standard disclaimer sentence (Legal asked for consistency): “Benchmark results reflect Redwood testing at the time of publication under the stated conditions; results may vary by workload, configuration, and region.”

Support Ops Bot: Logged: request to create/update Support macro for benchmark methodology + region variance response. Owner: Jasmine Liu. Status: In progress.
